summary: Beis Shammai say that something made hekdesh by mistake is still hekdesh, and Beis Hillel say it is not. For example, a man said the first black ox to come out would be hekdesh, and a white one came out.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: hekdesh made by mistake is still hekdesh.
chunks.st: Consecration that one performs in error nevertheless renders property consecrated,

words.note: Something given to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say

chunks.en: it is not hekdesh.
chunks.st: it is not consecrated.

chunks.en: How is it? He said,
chunks.st: How so; what is considered an act of erroneous consecration? If one said:

chunks.en: "The black ox that comes out of my house
chunks.st: A black bull that will emerge from my house

chunks.en: first will be hekdesh,"
chunks.st: first is consecrated,

chunks.en: and a white one came out.
chunks.st: and a white bull emerged first,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is hekdesh,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say it is consecrated

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is not hekdesh.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say it is not consecrated.

summary: More examples of hekdesh by mistake: he said a gold coin, and a silver one came up; he said a barrel of wine, and a barrel of oil came up.

chunks.en: "The gold dinar that comes up in my hand
chunks.st: Similarly, if one said: A gold dinar that will come up first in my hand

chunks.en: first will be hekdesh,"
chunks.st: is consecrated,

chunks.en: and a silver one came up:
chunks.st: and when he reached into his pocket a dinar of silver came up,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is hekdesh,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say it is consecrated

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is not hekdesh.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say it is not consecrated.

chunks.en: "The barrel of wine that comes up in my hand
chunks.st: Likewise, if one said: A barrel of wine that will come up first in my hand

chunks.en: first will be hekdesh,"
chunks.st: when I enter the cellar is consecrated,

chunks.en: and a barrel of oil came up:
chunks.st: and a barrel of oil came up in his hand instead,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is hekdesh,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say it is consecrated

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is not hekdesh.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say it is not consecrated.

summary: If a Sage undoes someone's nezirus, the animal he set aside becomes a plain animal again. Beis Hillel use this to argue with Beis Shammai about hekdesh made by mistake, and Beis Shammai answer with the animals of maaser.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁנָּדַר בְּנָזִיר וְנִשְׁאַל לְחָכָם וַאֲסָרוֹ,
chunks.en: Someone who promised to be a nazir asked a Sage, and the Sage said he must keep it:
chunks.explain: He had stopped keeping it, hoping it would be undone.
chunks.st: With regard to one who took a vow of naziriteship, who then regretted his vow and stopped observing the prohibition against drinking wine, and later requested of a halakhic authority to dissolve his vow, and the authority ruled that he is bound by his vow, finding no reason to dissolve it,

chunks.en: he counts from the time he made the promise.
chunks.st: he counts the term of naziriteship from the time that he vowed,
chunks.stMore: including the days when he acted as though the vow were dissolved.

chunks.en: If he asked a Sage and the Sage undid it,
chunks.st: In a case where he requested of a halakhic authority to dissolve his vow and the authority dissolved it,

chunks.en: if he had an animal set aside,
chunks.st: if he had an animal separated as a nazirite offering

chunks.en: it goes out and grazes with the flock.
chunks.st: it shall go out and graze among the flock.
chunks.stMore: On the basis of this halakha, and continuing their discussion in the previous mishna,

chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to Beis Shammai,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

chunks.en: "Don't you agree in this case
chunks.st: Don’t you concede with regard to this case

chunks.en: that it is hekdesh by mistake,
chunks.st: that it is an erroneous act of consecration,

chunks.en: and it goes out and grazes with the flock?"
chunks.st: and yet the halakha is that it shall go out and graze among the flock?
chunks.stMore: This shows that you too accept the principle that an erroneous act of consecration does not take effect.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:

chunks.en: "Don't you agree about someone who made a mistake
chunks.explain: He was counting his animals to make every tenth one maaser.
chunks.st: Don’t you concede with regard to one who was separating the animal tithe from his herd, i.e., passing his animals before him single file and consecrating every tenth one as a tithe, that if he erred

chunks.en: and called the ninth "tenth," and the tenth "ninth,"
chunks.st: and called the ninth animal: Tenth; and the tenth: Ninth;

chunks.en: and the eleventh "tenth,"
chunks.st: and the eleventh: Tenth,

chunks.en: that it is holy?"
chunks.explain: This shows that hekdesh by mistake counts.
chunks.st: that each of them is consecrated?
chunks.stMore: This proves that an erroneous act of consecration does take effect.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to them:

chunks.en: "It is not the stick that makes it holy.
chunks.explain: He counted the animals with a stick.
chunks.st: It is not the rod that consecrates it.
chunks.stMore: The touch of the rod does not consecrate the animal, nor does the fact that he said: Tenth, by mistake. Not all errors cause the tithe to be consecrated, and the proof is as follows:

chunks.he: וּמָה אִלּוּ טָעָה וְהִנִּיחַ אֶת הַשֵּׁבֶט
chunks.en: What if he made a mistake and put the stick
chunks.st: And what would be the halakha if he had erred and placed the rod

chunks.en: on the eighth or the twelfth?
chunks.st: on the eighth or on the twelfth, and labeled them: Tenth?

chunks.en: Did he do anything?
chunks.explain: The eighth or the twelfth does not become maaser.
chunks.st: Can it be suggested that perhaps he performed anything
chunks.stMore: of consequence? The halakha is that the eighth or twelfth animal cannot be consecrated as tithe.

chunks.en: Rather, the same pasuk that made the tenth holy
chunks.st: Rather, why is the ninth or eleventh animal consecrated? There is a specific reason for this halakha, as the same verse that consecrated the tenth

chunks.en: made the ninth holy
chunks.st: also consecrated the ninth

chunks.en: and the eleventh."
chunks.st: and the eleventh.
chunks.stMore: It is a Torah edict that the consecration takes effect with regard to those two animals. Therefore, one cannot infer from this case that an erroneous act of consecration takes effect.

summary: A man promised to be a nazir and then found that the animal for his korban was stolen. The mishnah teaches when this undoes his promise, and tells how Nachum HaMadi made a mistake about nazirs after the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed.

chunks.en: Someone who promised to be a nazir
chunks.st: With regard to one who took a vow of naziriteship

chunks.en: and went to bring his animal,
chunks.st: and went to bring his animal which he set aside for his nazirite offering

chunks.en: and found that it was stolen:
chunks.st: and discovered that it was stolen,
chunks.stMore: and due to the need to separate an additional animal now regrets having taken his vow,

chunks.he: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְנְבָה בְהֶמְתּוֹ נָזַר,
chunks.en: if he made the promise before his animal was stolen,
chunks.st: if he took a vow of naziriteship before his animal was stolen,

chunks.en: he is a nazir.
chunks.st: he is a nazirite,
chunks.stMore: as a vow cannot be dissolved as the result of a later event.

chunks.en: But if he made the promise after his animal was stolen,
chunks.st: But if he took a vow of naziriteship after his animal was stolen,

chunks.en: he is not a nazir.
chunks.explain: He promised by mistake, counting on an animal he did not have.
chunks.st: he is not a nazirite,
chunks.stMore: as it is retroactively established that his vow was taken in error from the outset, as he relied on an animal he did not possess.

chunks.en: This was the mistake that Nachum HaMadi made.
chunks.st: And this was the error that Naḥum the Mede erred
chunks.stMore: when he failed to distinguish between an event that occurred before the vow was taken and an event that occurred afterward.

words.note: Nachum from the land of Madai.

chunks.en: When nazirs came up from the exile
chunks.st: The incident in question was as follows: When nazirites were ascending from the exile to sacrifice their offerings,

chunks.en: and found the Beis HaMikdash destroyed,
chunks.st: and they found the Temple destroyed,

chunks.en: Nachum HaMadi said to them,
chunks.st: Naḥum the Mede said to them:

chunks.en: "If you had known
chunks.st: If you had known

chunks.en: that the Beis HaMikdash would be destroyed,
chunks.st: that the Temple would be destroyed,

chunks.en: would you have become nazirs?"
chunks.st: would you have taken a vow of naziriteship?

chunks.en: They said to him, "No."
chunks.st: They said to him: Certainly not,
chunks.stMore: as there is no remedy for a naziriteship in this case.

chunks.en: So Nachum HaMadi undid their promises.
chunks.st: And Naḥum the Mede dissolved the vow for them.

chunks.en: When the matter came before the Sages,
chunks.st: And when the matter came before the Rabbis,

chunks.en: they said to him,
chunks.st: they said: His ruling is incorrect. Rather,

chunks.en: "Whoever became a nazir
chunks.st: whoever took a vow of naziriteship

chunks.en: before the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed
chunks.st: before the Temple was destroyed,

chunks.en: is a nazir.
chunks.explain: He made no mistake when he promised.
chunks.st: like these nazirites from the exile, he is a nazirite,
chunks.stMore: as he committed no error at the time of his vow, and one cannot dissolve vows based a new situation.

chunks.en: But whoever promised after the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed
chunks.st: However, one who stated his vow after the Temple was destroyed

chunks.en: is not a nazir."
chunks.st: is not a nazirite, as he vowed based on an erroneous assumption.

summary: People on the road saw someone coming and made nezirus promises about who he was. Beis Shammai say they are all nazirs, Beis Hillel say only some, and Rabbi Tarfon says none of them.

chunks.he: הָיוּ מְהַלְּכִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְאֶחָד בָּא כְנֶגְדָּן,
chunks.en: People were walking on the road, and someone came toward them.
chunks.st: If there were people walking along the way, and one other person was approaching them,

chunks.en: One of them said,
chunks.st: and one of those walking said:

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if this is so-and-so."
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite if this person approaching us is so-and-so.

chunks.en: And another said,
chunks.st: And another one of them said:

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if this is not so-and-so."
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite if this is not so-and-so,

chunks.en: Another said, "I am a nazir if one of you is a nazir,"
chunks.st: while a third member of the group said: I am hereby a nazirite if one of you two is a nazirite,

chunks.en: "if neither of you is a nazir,"
chunks.st: and a fourth said: I am hereby a nazirite if neither of you is a nazirite,

chunks.en: "if both of you are nazirs,"
chunks.st: and another added: I am hereby a nazirite if both of you are nazirites.

chunks.en: "if all of you are nazirs."
chunks.st: Finally, the last person said: I am hereby a nazirite if all you who spoke before me are nazirites.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say they are all nazirs.
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say that they are all nazirites,
chunks.stMore: as by saying: I am hereby a nazirite, they have accepted naziriteship upon themselves even if their statements turn out to be incorrect. Beit Shammai maintain that a vow of naziriteship taken in error is considered a valid vow of naziriteship.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: only the one
chunks.st: Only he whose

chunks.en: whose words did not come true is a nazir.
chunks.st: statement was not fulfilled is a nazirite.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Tarfon says:

chunks.en: not one of them is a nazir.
chunks.explain: None of them knew for sure who was coming.
chunks.st: Not a single one of them is a nazirite,
chunks.stMore: including those whose statements were correct. Rabbi Tarfon maintains that a vow of naziriteship must be pronounced in an explicit manner, without any hint of uncertainty. In this case, none of them knew for sure the identity of the person coming toward them, and therefore they could not be certain they were nazirites at the time of their vows.

summary: If the person turned back and they never found out who he was, none of them is a nazir. Rabbi Shimon says each one should keep nezirus with a condition.

chunks.en: If he turned back,
chunks.explain: So they never found out who he was.
chunks.st: If the person approaching them turned back so that his identity was never discovered,

chunks.en: none of them is a nazir.
chunks.st: not one of them is a nazirite.
chunks.stMore: The matter was never clarified, and the halakha is lenient in cases of uncertain naziriteship.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says
chunks.stMore: that the halakha is stringent with regard to an uncertainty of this kind, and therefore they should proceed as follows in order to avoid any uncertainty:

chunks.en: each should say, "If it was like I said,
chunks.st: Each of those who took a vow should say: If it was in accordance with my statement,

chunks.en: I am a nazir because I have to be.
chunks.st: I am hereby an obligatory nazirite, as my condition was fulfilled,

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if not,

chunks.en: I am a nazir by my own choice."
chunks.st: I am hereby a voluntary nazirite,
chunks.stMore: and in this manner they are all nazirites either way.

summary: People saw a koy, an animal that is partly like a wild animal and partly like a farm animal, and each one made a nezirus promise about what it is. They all become nazirs.

chunks.en: Someone saw a koy and said,
chunks.st: Someone saw a kosher animal with characteristics of both a domesticated animal and a non-domesticated animal [koy], and said:

words.note: An animal that is partly like a wild animal and partly like a farm animal.

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if this is a wild animal."
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite if this is a non-domesticated animal; and another individual said:

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if this is not a wild animal."
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite if this is not a non-domesticated animal; and a third person said:

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if this is a farm animal."
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite if this is a domesticated animal; and a fourth said:

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if this is not a farm animal."
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite if this not a domesticated animal. The mishna continues: A fifth person added:

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if this is a wild animal and a farm animal."
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite if this is a non-domesticated animal and a domesticated animal,

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if this is
chunks.st: and a sixth person said: I am hereby a nazirite if this is

chunks.en: neither a wild animal nor a farm animal."
chunks.st: neither a non-domesticated animal nor a domesticated animal.

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if one of you is a nazir,"
chunks.st: Someone who heard all the above statements said: I am hereby a nazirite if one of you is a nazirite,

chunks.he: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שֶׁאֵין אֶחָד מִכֶּם נָזִיר,
chunks.en: "I am a nazir if not one of you is a nazir,"
chunks.st: and another one stated: I am hereby a nazirite if not one of you is a nazirite,

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if all of you are nazirs,"
chunks.st: and a final person said: I am hereby a nazirite if all of you are nazirites.

chunks.en: they are all nazirs.
chunks.st: In this case, they are all nazirites.
